generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: 'WELCOME TO THE AGI ERA': OPENAI LAUNCHES GPT-6 ASTRA
Summary: OpenAI claims its newly released frontier model, GPT-6 Astra, likely marks the onset of artificial general intelligence. The promotional video OpenAI released for the model shows various OpenAI employees interacting with computer interfaces using Astra through voice. Astra is now rolling out to enterprise customers through OpenAI's gated access program, Daybreak. It will become available over the coming days to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise customers, as well as through the OpenAI API and cloud platforms, including AWS Bedrock and Microsoft Azure.

Editorial idea:
A claimed arrival of general intelligence turns ordinary computer interaction into a threshold moment: people are still directing the system, but the system is beginning to mediate the work.

Central subject:
The transition from human-operated software to an AI system acting through computer interfaces.

Visual relationship:
Human agency remains visibly present while the new model occupies the intermediate space between intention and execution.

Composition:
A person stands at one side of a doorway-like work surface, extending a hand toward a sequence of interface panels that continue beyond the threshold; the human side is orderly and familiar, while the far side is active but only partially revealed, making the threshold itself the focal point.

Permitted literal elements:
one person interacting with a computer interface
a clear doorway or threshold
several interface panels without rendered text
subtle visual continuity from the person's gesture into the interface activity

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
racks
chips
laptops as the central subject
robots
clouds
shields
arrows
charts
skyscrapers
chess
handshakes
split-screen conflict
logos
rendered text
artist imitation
unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
depicting a generic futuristic AI instead of the reported computer-interface use
making the model appear fully autonomous when the summary describes employees interacting with it
using decorative sci-fi machinery without factual grounding
turning the threshold into a literal product launch stage

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
